summary: H. Munro Chadwick worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Clare College and Cambridge (BA 1892, MA ~1896) under Wilhelm Streitberg. He served as Cambridge's Elrington and Bosworth Professor of Anglo-Saxon (1910–1941).
H. Schöhl worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Freiburg, Munich, Göttingen, Strasbourg (~1901–1905) under Ernst Leumann, and Münster (PhD 1914), and also studied under Richard Schmidt.
H. Sesha Aiyangar was an Indologist and linguist who held posts at the University of Madras in the Kannaḍa Department (attested 1938) and the Canarese Department (attested 1957).
H. V. Nagaraja Rao worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
Hae-ju Sunim worked in Buddhist studies. She was a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied under Zhongxin Jiang and Kemo Jin at Peking University (MA 1982), and served as Director at the University of Freiburg in 2010.

Hajime Kitamura was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Shizuoka High School and the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. He held posts at NINJAL, the University of Tokyo, TUFS, Toyo Bunko, and was president of Reitaku University (1986).

Hajime Nakamura specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui, later serving there as professor (1954–1973). He also founded Toho Gakuin and served as its director (~1973–1999).

Hajime Okayama worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, and in Beijing under Xianlin Ji. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia and was professor at Tokyo (1995–2012).

Hajime Sakurabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Otani University, studying under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, and served as professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1960) and Otani University (1971–1986).

Hajime Tanabe was a philosopher who studied at Tokyo and Kyoto, as well as in Germany under Heidegger, Rickert, and Husserl, and under Kitaro Nishida. He held posts at Tohoku University and Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Dōkyō Etan (~1708) and Hakuyūshi (~1710–1711).

Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu at Tokyo, and in Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, Nagoya, and served as president of Komazawa University (1941).

Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Toshima Normal School and trained under several teachers, notably Sogaku Harada (1925–1943). In 1954, he founded Sanbo Zen.

Hakuyu Hadano worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at Tohoku University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1953–1959) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026).
Halina Marlewicz works in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Tadeusz Pobożniak and holds a post as professor at Jagiellonian University.
Halina Safarewiczowa was a linguist who studied at Vilnius University (~1923–1928) and held a post at Jagiellonian University (~1945–1974).

Halle O'Neal works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler (attested 2011) and serves as Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Hallvard Kåre Kuløy worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as an officer for UNICEF (1972–1978, 1980–1984), edited Kailash (~1973–1985), and founded Orchid Press and Bibliotheca Himalayica in 1982.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Vidyodaya Pirivena, Banaras Hindu University, and Edinburgh (PhD). He taught at Vikramashila Pirivena, BHU, SOAS, and Toronto, and headed the London Buddhist Vihara (~1957–1990).
